## The single objection most likely to be right

**OBJ-12/OBJ-16 (cluster 4): the model under test is not on the path.** Answer it first, because every other objection about the L1 page is downstream of it. If the constant per-poll hazard has drawn no fill since aeeaae36 (2026-08-10) — and the evidence is a single production call site behind a config flag that is `false`, a config_guard WARN if anyone sets it true, and a shipped pin (`test_sim_fill_queue.py:190-213`) that calls the branch "a dead control" in as many words — then the ceiling defect (cluster 3), the horizon defect (OBJ-13), the composition defects (clusters 6-8) and the p_sim column (cluster 10) are all defects in an instrument that was answering a question nobody has been asking for 35 days. It is also the cheapest to settle: one `grep _passive_poll_prob` and one read of config.json:399 either confirms or refutes it, with no store, no ring drift, and no statistics. It is the CLAUDE.md invariant-3 recurrence exactly ("the router is constructed and never read"), and the page's own same-day audit addendum, written after a 34-agent pass, missed it — which is the strongest signal on this docket that the instrument, not the market, is the thing that is wrong.

OBJ-3 is the most likely to be right AND the most dangerous (it is on a safety claim in an unpushed commit message), but it is independent of the page and is answered by one injection the panel has already run twice. Do it second, before push.

## What the panel could NOT assess

- **The subject itself.** No panelist read a diff, because there is none; all readings are of the untracked page, the committed generator, and baad9754. If the author intended a different tree or commit, every finding above must be re-mapped (OBJ-2).
- **The 10:33Z corpus.** The recordings ring is a live 60-file FIFO at cap; it moved from 282 to 289 tapes between the page's generation and the panel's reads (10744/389 → 10764/395 at 5 bps). No panelist re-ran the generator end to end; all numbers come from the generator's own component functions over the live store, snapshot-stamped 23:50Z-00:09Z. The page's printed rows are unrecoverable and were reproduced arithmetically, not observed.
- **The addendum's own provenance.** Lines 50-51 appeared between two reads (49→51) at mtime 18:48:38 -0500, 85 s after baad9754's commit time; the panel could not see who wrote them or whether they were still being edited after the last read.
- **WS/REST book plumbing beyond the source.** OBJ-18's staleness-conditioning mechanism rests on `kraken_max_book_age_sec=3.5 < polling_interval_sec=5` and runner.py:256-259's own comment; no panelist logged WS update cadence or traced FeedRecorder at runtime, and the running process was not queried for the config it booted.
- **Effective-n magnitude.** Two DEFF routes disagree (96.8 vs 75.1; n_eff 111 vs 143); both are level-based approximations of the design effect on the LR shape statistic, and the five "clusters" are optimistically counted (three share one session, so m ≈ 3 and cluster-robust p has 2-4 dof). Direction is settled; magnitude is not.
- **The 10 and 15 bps life tables.** Never printed by the page; per-bucket first-poll claims at those buckets are unverified and were dropped from OBJ-14.
- **Smoke construction duration.** OBJ-3's queue-drain arm is a race between one `consume()` and the live runner's 5 s poll; the panel measured that the drain happens, not how wide the window is under a real engine build.
- **The 09-13 19:57:28 rewrite of all nine prior report files** (identical mtimes) — noticed, unexplained, possibly the resume-storm checkout; irrelevant to any ruling but not resolved.
- **Whether the learning-panel scheduled task actually fired on 09-15.** The "tomorrow's page regenerates without the addendum" leg of OBJ-1/4/11 assumes the 10:30Z task runs; the schtasks query returned nothing through the panel's shell (a broken scan, not evidence either way) and one panelist read the trigger from another route.
- **Fixture-file vs sidecar reconciliation** (7 tapes × 2 frames per file vs 199 tapes / 46 sidecars): not reconciled; not load-bearing.
- **Whether `fill_hazard_report.py:80`'s "~12-188 ms" burst rationale (2026-07-31) was ever observed on real tapes** — dropped as unverified; flagged for the author.
